title: Telomere length assessments of muscle stem cells in rodent and human skeletal muscle sections
protocol: Remove one slide from each desired sample set from −20°C and warm to room temperature.
Immerse slides in 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS for 10 minutes.
Wash slides twice with PBS for 3 minutes each.
Heat TET buffer to boiling in a microwave.
Transfer hot TET buffer to a coplin jar placed in a preheated steamer (95°–100°C).
Add slides to the coplin jar containing hot TET buffer and incubate for 10 minutes.
Let the coplin jar cool at room temperature for 15 minutes after removing it from the steamer.
Wash slides with PBS twice for 3 minutes each.
Remove slides from coplin jar.
Mark tissue boundaries with a hydrophobic/PAP pen.
Add sufficient RNase A (100 μg/mL) to cover tissue on the slide.
Cover the slide with a glass coverslip to prevent evaporation.
Incubate slides at 37°C in a slide warmer or alternative heating source for 20 min.
Remove coverslip and transfer slides into coplin jars containing PBS.
Wash slides twice for 3 min each at room temperature (25°C).
Prepare hybridization buffer as described in the materials and equipment section.
Vortex and pipette extensively to get all components completely into solution.
Prepare TelC-Alexa Fluor 647 telomere probe by diluting 5 nmol probe pellet with 100 μL formamide.
Aliquot in 4 μL aliquots in 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes and store at -80°C.
Remove telomere probe from −80°C storage, thaw the probe.
Add probe at a 1/600 dilution to the hybridization buffer (1.67 μL/mL of buffer).
Heat probe(s) in hybridization buffer for 10 min at 67°C in the dark.
Add hybridization buffer containing probe to slides.
Cover slides with a glass coverslip to prevent evaporation during incubation.
Incubate slides in a Thermobrite slide warmer or equivalent heating source according to specified conditions.
Preheat wash buffers I, II, III, IV to 55°C in a water bath or equivalent heating source.
Gently remove coverslips from slides after hybridization.
Place slides in coplin jars.
Incubate slides with 50 mL prewarmed wash buffer I for 5 min at 55°C.
Repeat wash once with 50 mL prewarmed wash buffer I.
Wash slides twice with 50 mL wash buffer II, 5 min each at 55°C.
Wash slides twice with 50 mL wash buffer III, 5 min each at 55°C.
Wash slides twice with 50 mL wash buffer IV, 5 min each at 55°C.
Wash slides once with PBS for 5 min at room temperature (25°C).
Block sections in 50 mL antibody blocking buffer for 1 h at room temperature (25°C).
Incubate slides in cold (4°C) blocking buffer with VCAM antibody (1/100 dilution); stock antibody concentration 1 mg/mL; use 100 μL of antibody solution per slide.
Cover slides with a coverslip to ensure even coverage of antibody solution.
Incubate overnight (16 h) in a dark, humidified staining chamber at 4°C.
Wash slides the following day twice with PBS for 5 min each at room temperature (25°C).

Incubate sections for 1 h with secondary antibody (Alexa Fluor 488 Donkey anti-goat IgG; 1/300 dilution) in antibody blocking buffer at room temperature (25°C); use 100 μL of antibody solution per slide.
Cover slides with a coverslip to ensure even coverage of antibody solution.
Wash slides three times for 5 min each with PBS at room temperature (25°C).
Mount coverslips with Prolong gold with DAPI.
Allow mounting media to solidify overnight at room temperature in the dark.
Image acquisition must take place as soon as possible after staining.
Complete imaging of all samples within 3 days or less.
Identify VCAM+ cells present in tissue sections using a Nikon Eclipse NiU widefield epifluorescence microscope.
Only image MuSCs in the satellite cell position between the basal lamina and the sarcolemma.
Switch to a higher-powered 100× objective.
Identify the optimal exposure settings for DAPI.
Determine the optimal exposure settings for telomere Alexa Fluor 647 signal.
Set the optimal exposure settings for optional centromere Cy3 imaging.
Do not change intensity settings once determined for the duration of the experiment.
Proceed with multichannel imaging of VCAM.
Capture DAPI images during multichannel imaging.
Image telomeres during multichannel imaging.
Optionally image centromeres during multichannel imaging.
Identify focal planes containing the most telomere signals for every cell of interest.
Image a minimum of 35 VCAM+ cells per biological sample.
Save multichannel images in raw file formats to maintain metadata.
Image as many cells as possible during scheduled equipment usage hours from the biological samples.
Ensure that more than one muscle section is examined per slide.
If imaging cannot be completed in one day, stagger genotypes/treatments during imaging sessions.
Avoid imaging cells positioned on top of or below other cells/nuclei to prevent confounding datasets.
Export raw image files in two groups as grayscale/monochrome 16-bit .tiff images for analysis.
Export a merged 8-bit color .tiff image to identify cells of interest (VCAM+) for later analysis.
Open Telometer software and create a new project in the “Admin” tab.
Identify cells of interest using the semi-automated ImageJ-based platform.
Measure the intensity of telomeres relative to the total DAPI intensity of each cell.
Normalize the total sum intensity of telomeres to DAPI intensity for cell cycle position variation.
Measure the mean intensity of telomeres and normalize it to DAPI intensity.
If nuclear architecture or staining is compromised, measure centromere intensities instead of telomere intensities.
Calculate the ratio of telomere measurements normalized to centromere intensities when necessary.
Select the Project name for your analysis grouping and the Preset objective.
Subtract Cy3 background.
Open the Telomere 16-bit monochrome exported tiff image when prompted.
Normalize the Telomere image by clicking and forming a box of any size in an area absent of features and click “normalize”.
Open the DAPI 16-bit monochrome exported tiff image when prompted.
Normalize the DAPI image by clicking and forming a box of any size in an area absent of features and click “normalize”.
Create masked images to narrow down regions in the image that contain telomere foci.
Threshold the masked image, if necessary, to obtain the greatest telomere foci in the image with the least background.
Manually draw a circle encompassing a nucleus of interest when prompted.
Refer to the color image to determine which nuclei are clearly VCAM+ and designate the nucleus of interest.
Select the “+ Add Nucleus” button.
Repeat for additional VCAM+ cells in the image, if any.
Click the “next” button.
Optionally separate conjoined telomere foci (if counting telomere number).
Manually remove halo artifacts from out of focus light.
Select “complete.”
Export data to copy into excel.
In the “Export” tab of Telometer, select the project name for data export.
Click the “Scoring” button that has an arrow.
Select all data under “Scorings”.
Click the “Cells” button that has an arrow.
Select all data under “Cells” and copy.
Paste the selected data into Excel or other spreadsheet software.
Note the headings for each column.
To analyze datasets using the Telomere sum option, refer to the last column of the dataset.
Calculate telomere mean intensities by dividing the datasets in the Telomere Mean column by its respective DAPI Sum (optional).
Normalize to centromere intensity instead of DAPI intensity if desired.
Open centromere images and name them similarly to the telomere analysis nuclei.
Select nuclei in the same order as the telomere analysis for centromere data.
Divide the last column of telomere analysis by the last column of centromere data analysis.
Graph datasets in Graphpad prism as total intensity values or histograms.
